claim_text: GitHub opened a status incident at 10:55 AM ET on Nov 25 for degraded experiences across its products
summary: GitHub's status page opened an incident, 'Investigating degraded experiences across GitHub products', at 10:55 AM ET (15:55 UTC) on Wednesday, Nov 25. The first update reported degraded performance for Actions and Webhooks.
detail: Within about 15 minutes the page listed Pull Requests, Pages, Issues, Git Operations, Actions and Packages with degraded availability or performance. GitHub's status feed rates the incident's impact as critical, the highest of its levels. Times are the status page's own, converted from UTC.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: GitHub's own status page and its public incident feed give the incident, its start time and its updates.

claim_text: The incident affected Git Operations, Webhooks, API Requests, Issues, Pull Requests, Actions, Packages and Pages
summary: GitHub lists eight affected parts of its service: Git Operations, Webhooks, API Requests, Issues, Pull Requests, Actions, Packages and Pages. Several were listed with degraded availability, not only slowness.
detail: Degraded availability means some requests failed; degraded performance means they were slow. GitHub has not said what share of requests failed or how many users were hit.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The incident page says 'This incident affected' and names the eight components; the feed gives each component's state as it changed.

claim_text: GitHub said the failures were caused by high database load and that it recovered by changing how that load was spread
summary: At 11:14 AM ET GitHub said it was investigating increased failures 'due to high database load' and working to reduce the load. At 11:25 AM ET it said it had 'updated our database load distribution' and was starting to see recovery.
detail: This is GitHub's own account of the immediate cause. It has not said what drove the database load up, and its closing update promises 'a detailed root cause analysis'.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The two updates are on GitHub's incident page and in its public feed, in those words.

claim_text: GitHub marked the incident resolved at 11:52 AM ET on Nov 25 and said a root cause analysis would follow
summary: GitHub marked the incident resolved at 11:52 AM ET (16:52 UTC), just under an hour after it opened. It said 'a detailed root cause analysis will be shared as soon as it is available.'
detail: GitHub moved the incident to monitoring at 11:36 AM ET, saying the degradation had been mitigated. At our check at 9:28 PM ET on Nov 25, GitHub's status page showed all systems operational. No root cause analysis was posted yet.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The resolved state, its time and the closing wording are on GitHub's incident page and feed; the status API reads 'All Systems Operational'.

claim_text: GitHub has said the Nov 25 outage was an attack
summary: GitHub has not said the outage was an attack. Its status updates name high database load and do not use the words attack, breach or hack. They do not rule out an attack either.
detail: The status updates describe the symptoms, the load on the database and the fix. GitHub has not said what caused the load.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Nothing on GitHub's incident page or feed points to a security cause, and nothing there says one was ruled out.

claim_text: Anyone has claimed responsibility for the Nov 25 GitHub outage
summary: We found no claim of responsibility and no report from an outside researcher, authority or news outlet saying the outage was an attack.
detail: We found no news outlet's own report on this outage at our check; pages about it repeat GitHub's status updates.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: GitHub's account names no attacker, and the public discussion we read treats it as a reliability problem.

claim_text: Later on Nov 25, Git Large File Storage was degraded for about three hours, which GitHub put down to a large volume of automated, unauthenticated traffic
summary: In a separate incident, GitHub says Git Large File Storage (LFS) was degraded from 4:30 to 7:28 PM ET, with up to 4% of requests failing. It says 'a large volume of automated, unauthenticated traffic' overwhelmed LFS servers in one region.
detail: On average 2% of LFS requests failed, peaking at 4%. GitHub says other Git operations were not affected. It fixed it by moving most LFS traffic to other regions, and says it is working to limit the impact of high-volume unauthenticated traffic and to add capacity. It marked this incident resolved at 7:43 PM ET.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: GitHub's own incident write-up gives the times, the failure rates, the cause in its words and the fix.

claim_text: The automated traffic behind the Git LFS slowdown was an attack
summary: GitHub calls it 'a large volume of automated, unauthenticated traffic'. It does not call it an attack and does not say who sent it or why.
detail: Heavy automated traffic can come from many sources, such as scrapers or misbehaving tools, and is not by itself evidence of an attack. GitHub has not said the LFS slowdown was linked to the morning outage.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: GitHub's write-up describes the traffic but not its source or purpose.

claim_text: Commenters suggest GitHub's push into AI is behind its outages
summary: In a Hacker News discussion of the outage, several commenters suggest that AI-written code or GitHub's AI features are behind its repeated outages. The thread is where the question is raised, not evidence for it.
detail: GitHub's own account of Nov 25 names high database load. Nothing GitHub has published links this outage to AI tools or AI-written code, and nothing public rules it out.
label: Rumor
why_it_supports: The thread shows the theory is going round; it gives no evidence for it.

claim_text: GitHub's status page lists other incidents this month; on Nov 19 it said a run of unexpected sign-outs was a bug and not a security incident
summary: GitHub's status feed shows other November incidents, among them unexpected sign-outs from Nov 5 to Nov 19 that GitHub said were 'caused by a bug in session renewal, not due to a security incident.' Its October report counts eight incidents.
detail: The list also includes a Copilot code-completion disruption late on Nov 24. These are separate incidents, listed to show how often GitHub reports problems; none of them is linked by GitHub to the Nov 25 outage.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: GitHub's own status feed and its monthly availability report state these incidents, dates and wording.
